dedupe_keys.name: fire statistics incident level datasets england

description: The fire statistics incident level datasets publish record-level data on incidents attended by fire and rescue services in England. They are released by the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government, which took over responsibility for fire and rescue from the Home Office on 1 April 2025; the collection page was first published in May 2021 and last updated on 22 July 2026. Separate datasets, each with guidance, cover dwelling fires, other building fires, domestic appliance fires, casualties in fires, fire-related fatalities, false alarms, outdoor and road vehicle fires, flooding and water rescue, non-fire incidents such as medical and collaborating incidents and road traffic collisions, daily incidents, fire stations and low-level geography. Coverage is England, with the larger series split into 2010-11 to 2016-17, 2017-18 to 2022-23 and 2023-24 to present. Access: OpenDocument spreadsheets on GOV.UK, alongside the aggregated fire statistics data tables updated with each release. Licence: Open Government Licence; free. Caveats: England only; spreadsheets were not opened, so fields come from dataset titles. Simulation uses: building fire frequencies and casualty rates for risk models and fire service planning. Related records: the England and Wales energy performance certificates.
